title: Vanderbilt 2K27: If the ’Dores were in a video game
dek: What would Vanderbilt Men’s Basketball’s roster look like if it were put into a video game?
author: Tristan Rutman
intro: If you're a big fan of Vanderbilt Men’s Basketball, you probably have a self-constructed hierarchy of players that you keep in the back of your mind. “Tyler Tanner is obviously our best player,” you might think to yourself, “but who comes next?”
That's a tough question to answer, especially with an almost entirely brand-new roster — with the exception of Tanner, Chandler Bing and Jayden Leverett.

Premier transfers Ace Glass, Bangot Dak, Berke Buyuktuncel and Sebastian Williams-Adams — among others — are ready to don the Black and Gold for the 2026-27 season. But what should fans expect from these players, and as a whole, this team?

Head coach Mark Byington came in two years ago and won more than double the number of games that former head coach Jerry Stackhouse won in his final season. Byington then one-upped himself a year later, recording the most regular season wins in Vanderbilt history. He did this all with just 10.4% of minute continuity in 2024-25 and only three significant players returning for 2025-26.
Byington is an impressive coach with an impressive resume, no doubt. But what’s the ceiling of this team?

The ’Dores’ ceiling is dependent on how well its players can perform, regardless of Byington’s coaching pedigree. Given that, I wanted to quantitatively determine what Commodore Faithful can expect from this roster.

I’ve taken the past few weeks to create a video game-style rating system for this season’s Vanderbilt Commodores. conclusion: These are subjective ratings, so there will certainly be room for disagreement. Overall, though, I hope this helps paint a picture of what to expect from each Commodore in the upcoming season.
